questions.question: When is it worth making a commit?

options.text: Before a big change and whenever something works
options.explanation: Correct. Then it’s easy to go back if the next change fails.

options.text: Only once, when the whole project is finished
options.explanation: Then you can’t go back to the steps in between. Commit often.
Claude can’t see the content of earlier conversations, and /rewind doesn’t replace Git.

questions.question: In which order are the commands run?

options.explanation: Exactly. First you choose the changes, then you make the checkpoint.
A commit only saves the chosen changes, so git add comes first.
These show the history and restore a file. A checkpoint is made with the commands git add and git commit.
